source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Lebanon, Ohio campus publishes 12 megawatts of IT capacity, the largest figure among Ohio data centers that report power, and modest against the multi-hundred-megawatt clusters AI training now requires.

Ohio's published data center load totals 60.4 megawatts across 77 mapped facilities, and this one site accounts for 20 percent of it. Only 8 of those 77 facilities report power figures at all, so the state total reflects a reporting minority rather than the load actually on the grid. The 400,000 square feet of technical space against 12 megawatts works out to roughly 300 racks at 40 kilowatts per rack, which is a density assumption rather than a published specification.

The certifications, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes, qualify the campus for regulated healthcare, finance, and federal workloads. That is a compliance position, not an AI position. The suitability score of 58 is built from published IT capacity and operator type, and it flags announced expansion as missing. Grid connection, power supply, expansion plans, tenants, and pricing are not published, so whether the grid serving Lebanon can sustain sustained high-density load at AI scale remains unstated.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
